text:
maria: Quick heads-up — int8 canary for raven-lite showed a small but consistent uptick in funcall parse errors after deploying the quantized checkpoint. Not a huge % yet (~0.6% -> 1.7%) but reproducible across batches. Logs attached in the canary run.

kevin: Ack. Which signal are we counting for 'parse error'? raw parse exceptions or JSON-schema rejects?

maria: Kevin: raw parse exceptions (json.loads) plus our schema linter marking missing required keys. I combined both for the overall "structured failure" metric.

sunil: Do we have a hypothesis? Tokenization/regression from quant kernels, or runtime truncation?

maria: Initial guess: subtle tokenization differences + trailing-token probability shifts that cause dangling commas / truncated brackets at the end of function-call outputs. But i've seen some full-strings that parse but fail schema (missing fields).

jess: Any chance mirrors (fp16 mirror runs) show the same?

maria: Mirrors (fp16) are clean in the canary. The delta appears only with the int8 run. Also traffic-weighted: the failures are more common when sequence length > 700.

kevin: Sounds like we should bisect on two axes: model float->quantized kernels and prompt/seqlength distribution. Proposal: run small focused experiments: 1) replay sample set of failing prompts across fp16/int8 with identical seeds 2) output token-level align diffs 3) run schema-conformance + parse-repair heuristics.

sunil: Agreed. Also add a parity-run with KV-cache disabled to rule out kvcache rounding.

maria: I'll draft a minimal plan. high-level: 
- sample 10k canary invocations that hit parse errors (slice by seqlen buckets)
- replay them deterministically across: fp16, int8-ptq, int8-perchannel (if available)
- capture: token stream, token ids, logits (head subset), and final text; compute per-token deviation metrics and edit-distance between outputs
- run schema linter and our "json-lens" repair attempt and record success rates
- measure latency/cost delta per variant

kevin: Nice. Can we get a lightweight probe that emits a short token-diff snippet like: 
```
{ "pos": 682, "fp16_token":"},\"", "int8_token":"},\" 
" }
```
so we can quickly eyeball off-by-one spaces vs control chars.

maria: yes. i'll include a token-diff microformat. Also plan to feed failing outputs into the rescue-layer (json-repair + trailing-brace heuristics) to see how much of the 1.7% is recoverable.

jess: Who owns collecting the samples and running the parity jobs? I can allocate a small canary cluster for replays if we have a job script.

maria: I can produce the sample set and baseline script today. Jess, if you can provision the canary cluster and give me a short-lived cred, i'll kick off runs.

kevin: We should also add a telemetry tag on the platform side so future int8 onboard runs automatically emit: model_variant, seqlen_bucket, parse_error_code, repair_success (bool). I'd rather have richer signals in our canary dashboards.

ops-bot: @maria created canary-job/7965432100-replay-probe (status: queued).

maria: thanks ops-bot. I'll attach the sample manifest here when ready.

sunil: One more idea: run a tiny ablation that forces deterministic sampling (topk=1 greedy) to see if sampling randomness amplifies the effect. If greedy still fails mostly on int8, that's a kernel/regression clue.

maria: good call. plan includes greedy / top-p=0.9 variants.

kevin: timeline?

maria: sample manifest in ~2h, replays should finish within the day on the small cluster, will post a short summary and token-diff examples. If the error is fixable by post-process repair for ~>60% of failures then we can ship a temporary mitigation while infra/quant team investigates.

jess: 👍 I'll provision the cluster now and share creds in DM.

canary-bot: Canary run started: canary-job-7965432100-replay-probe. Tracking at https://canary.redwood.internal/runs/7965432100

maria: thanks all — will update when we have the diff artifacts. If anyone wants to join the investigation loop, ping me and i'll add you to the run watchlist. :mag:
